ocr.notes: image has 'Hingland' (mock accent) where transcript has 'England'

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Republican reported that Tom Allen closed his Free and Easy on Washington Avenue, and that Ed. Donnelly, saying he was owed $125 for sparring and was knocked down when he asked, had Allen's trunks attached.

metadata.notes: masthead reads 'The St. Louis Republican, Wednesday Morning, April 12, 1876' (pg 8), kept as printed

facts.fact: Allen closed his Free and Easy on Washington Avenue and packed up, reportedly for a trip to England or the East
places: Free and Easy, Washington Avenue, St. Louis

facts.fact: Ed. Donnelly claimed Allen owed him $25 for each of five sparring exhibitions, said Allen knocked him down when he asked for money, and had Allen's trunks attached for $125 at Justice Walton's office
Allen asked police to arrest Donnelly for carrying off a coat; Donnelly went to the Third District station but nothing came of it
places: Third District police station, St. Louis

notes: the England trip is the paper's claim; Allen denied it the next day (articles 068, 069). existing_fact 000 = 'pay dispute with Ned Donnelly'
